title.sl: Kar ni bilo: if I'd known, I'd have come
title.de: Was nicht war: if I'd known, I'd have come
title.it: Ciò che non è stato: if I'd known, I'd have come
title.en: What wasn't so: if I'd known, I'd have come

rule.sl:
Kar se ni zgodilo in se ne da več spremeniti: **if** + **had** + deležnik, v drugem delu **would have** + deležnik: **If I had known, I would have come.** (Če bi {m:vedel|f:vedela}, bi {m:prišel|f:prišla}.) Nisem vedel{m:|f:a}, nisem {m:prišel|f:prišla}. Slovenščina ima tudi za to *če bi*.

Ljudje dvakrat rečejo **'d**: **If I'd known, I'd have come.** Prvi **'d** je **had** (za if), drugi **would** (pred have).

Zanikano **hadn't**, **wouldn't have**: **If it hadn't rained, we wouldn't have stayed.** Drugi del tudi **could have**, **might have**: **If you'd asked, I could have helped.**

V govoru je would have **would've**, sliši se kot *woulda*, zato ljudje pišejo tudi *would of*. Marsikdo reče tudi *If I'd have known* in *If I would have known*. Pisno velja **If I had known**, **would have**.

Primerjaj: **If I knew, I'd tell you.** (zdaj) **If I'd known, I'd have told you.** (takrat)
rule.de:
Was nicht geschehen ist und sich nicht mehr ändern lässt: **if** + **had** + Partizip, im anderen Teil **would have** + Partizip: **If I had known, I would have come.** (Wenn ich es gewusst hätte, wäre ich gekommen.) Immer have: nie *would be come*, auch wo Deutsch *wäre* sagt.

Man sagt zweimal **'d**: **If I'd known, I'd have come.** Das erste **'d** ist **had** (nach if), das zweite **would** (vor have).

Verneint **hadn't**, **wouldn't have**: **If it hadn't rained, we wouldn't have stayed.** Der andere Teil auch **could have**, **might have**: **If you'd asked, I could have helped.**

Gesprochen ist would have **would've**, es klingt wie *woulda*, darum schreibt man auch *would of*. Viele sagen auch *If I'd have known* und *If I would have known*. Geschrieben gilt **If I had known**, **would have**.

Vergleiche: **If I knew, I'd tell you.** (jetzt) **If I'd known, I'd have told you.** (damals)
rule.it:
Ciò che non è successo e non si può più cambiare: **if** + **had** + participio, **would have** + participio nell'altra parte: **If I had known, I would have come.** (Se l'avessi saputo, sarei venut{m:o|f:a}.) Sempre have: mai *would be come*, anche dove l'italiano dice *sarei*.

Si dice due volte **'d**: **If I'd known, I'd have come.** Il primo **'d** è **had** (dopo if), il secondo **would** (prima di have).

Al negativo **hadn't**, **wouldn't have**: **If it hadn't rained, we wouldn't have stayed.** L'altra parte anche **could have**, **might have**: **If you'd asked, I could have helped.**

A voce would have è **would've**, suona come *woulda*, perciò si scrive anche *would of*. Molti dicono anche *If I'd have known* e *If I would have known*. Per iscritto vale **If I had known**, **would have**.

Confronta: **If I knew, I'd tell you.** (ora) **If I'd known, I'd have told you.** (allora)
rule.en:
What didn't happen and can't change now: **if** + **had** + the participle, **would have** + the participle in the other half: **If I had known, I would have come.** (I didn't know, I didn't come.) Always have: *would be come* isn't English.

People say **'d** twice: **If I'd known, I'd have come.** The first **'d** is **had** (after if), the second **would** (before have).

With not: **hadn't**, **wouldn't have**: **If it hadn't rained, we wouldn't have stayed.** The other half also takes **could have**, **might have**: **If you'd asked, I could have helped.**

In talk would have is **would've**, it sounds like *woulda*, so people also write *would of*. Many also say *If I'd have known* and *If I would have known*. Writing wants **If I had known**, **would have**.

Compare: **If I knew, I'd tell you.** (now) **If I'd known, I'd have told you.** (then)
